v.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 4 is dead and has no effect.
Edge 2 carries nothing if node 1 receives no input from edge 0, so the edit is bypassed.
Node 2's output cannot reach node 3 without edge 5, so the edit on edge 2 is irrelevant.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, whose only exits are edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the edit is bypassed.
The edge 1 to node 2 path is cut off from the output when edge 5 is none, so the edit has little effect.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is dead, so removing edge 4 changes almost nothing, which is less harmful than removing it in a live cell.
Adding a direct 0->3 conv where none existed gives a large gain relative to swapping an existing op.
The direct conv on edge 3 makes a parallel conv on edge 5 more redundant, so the marginal gain is smaller.
A strong direct conv already supplies capacity to the output, so extra conv on edge 4 is partly redundant.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the direct edge loses more than deleting a pool or skip.
